brief: 011 C Step 2: the sliceable HUD kit (rounds 6 and 6b)
tool: No new image generation. Art is the Codex sheets listed under sources (all free, generated in rounds 5, 5b and 6; prompts, seconds and sha256 in their own PROVENANCE.json); sprites are cut, sliced, state-varied and drawn in code (out/concepts/ui-011-kit/build1.py, build2.py, build3.py, post.py). decisions.dock: left column, corner as a setting (roster_row), bottom kept as a third

panel_kit_pn_cab.prompt: Game interface concept art for a polished, shipped real-time tactics game, one flat landscape 3:2 image. World: an optimistic atompunk city in an alternate history, a 1950s world that discovered atomic power centuries ago, so its culture and style are 1950s but its technology is centuries ahead: clockwork, enamel and chrome instruments; never a touchscreen, hologram, glass blur or sci-fi neon. FINISH: professional AAA game HUD craftsmanship: crafted bevels, real enamel sheen with soft specular highlights, polished chrome trim with bright reflections, subtle depth, ambient occlusion and soft inner shadows, crisp edges, readable at 1080p; physical-object realism like a premium 3D-rendered control panel seen straight from the front. Palette: cream #f7f4ec and ivory #eee9da enamel, seafoam #72b5a7, deep teal #1f6c67, ink teal #17302f, polished chrome, a thin brass hairline only (never a large brass surface); turquoise #1cb9c6 only as a tiny indicator light. No red, no amber, no violet, no orange anywhere. Canvas rule: the whole canvas is one flat, perfectly even, solid magenta #ff00ff with no scene, no shadow, no gradient and no vignette; magenta never appears inside a piece. No text, no letters, no numerals, no logos anywhere on any piece. ROSTER STYLE: a TRAIN-CAB INSTRUMENT CLUSTER: a dark ink-teal satin panel with a polished chrome beaded edge, tiny chrome screws and a seafoam enamel stripe. Draw exactly FOUR separate pieces, each fully opaque, at least 60 px of magenta between them and from the edge, all flush rectangles with softly rounded corners, nothing sticking out. PIECE 1, top left: the DARK PANEL, about 640 px wide and 400 px tall: dark ink-teal satin enamel, a polished chrome beaded edge all round, four tiny chrome screws at its corners, interior one flat even satin dark teal, completely empty. PIECE 2, top right: the IVORY CARD, about 520 px wide and 400 px tall: ivory enamel with a thin polished chrome edge and soft rounded corners, a deep teal enamel header band across its top quarter with a fine chrome line under the band, the body one flat even ivory, completely empty. PIECE 3, bottom left: the SLIM STRIP, about 880 px wide and 110 px tall: a long slim dark ink-teal satin strip with a chrome beaded edge and rounded ends, completely empty. PIECE 4, bottom right: the TAB, a small stadium-shaped cream enamel plate about 300 px wide and 90 px tall with a polished chrome rim and a glossy face, completely empty.
panel_kit_pn_cab.use: text panel kit in the r04 cab finish: dark panel, ivory card with a teal header, slim strip, tab; nine-sliced in code for every panel in the HUD

hurt_portraits.prompt: Game character portrait. The attached reference image is the character: keep the SAME person, face, hair, costume, colours and trim, the same framing, crop, pose and camera distance, and the same flat light grey background. Change only the state: the character is HURT after a scuffle: hair and clothes dishevelled, scuffs and dust on the costume, a bruise on the cheekbone or jaw, a tired pained expression, the head slightly bowed or turned away, the straps and trim slightly out of place. No blood and no red: only dust, grey scuffs and dark bruises. No text, no frame, no border.
hurt_portraits.use: hurt-state portrait edited from Forma's normal portrait

portraits_note: Forma's white set for now. Portrait files are named portrait_<role>_<state>; swap by replacing those files (same size, same crop; the crop is head-and-shoulders, head centre x 0.5, y 0.42, zoom 1.12). Hurt portraits are the round 5b image-tool edits of Forma's portraits. Forma's round 4 L4 redesign can drop in.
fonts: Jost (display, OFL 1.1, instanced to Medium/SemiBold/Bold from the variable font with fontTools) and Barlow (body, OFL 1.1). The round 6 mock-ups used Futura and Avenir Next (not shippable): sizes were adjusted (Barlow body +0.5 to +1 px) but metrics differ, so text widths differ slightly from the concept frames. The OFL texts are in fonts/.

signal_check.colours: layout.json colors_delta_e: every named colour is at least dE 21.3 from cone red, guard amber and rival violet (brass 21.3, card-ivory 23.6; the card ivory is a sprite, not a flat colour)
signal_check.pixels: pixel_dE_note: for every exported @2x sprite, the share of opaque pixels within dE 20 of a signal colour. All panel, button, marker and overlay art is at 0.3% or less after a final pass that pulls any pixel closer than dE 22 toward neutral (post.py). Exempt by design: signal_* and mark_no (they are the signals), and the portraits and cameos (skin, hair and costume of people; 1 to 16% of a portrait's pixels sit within dE 20 of amber or red, as people do).

known_differences_from_the_concept_frame: verb plate is the plain strip (rounded ends, chrome bead) with the knobs as separate sprites; the concept's plate had cream end caps baked with its knobs

the roster column is 109 x 416 px (38.5% of the screen height) with 66 px windows; the round 6 anatomy sheet and notes said 119 x 453 and 42%, which was the 72 px-window size from an earlier pass. Strips start at x = 125
panels are sliced from small reference sprites; the dark panel's chrome and screw detail repeat at the corners only, so very large panels (briefing) show a plain interior, as the concept did
text is not baked into any sprite; numerals and labels are text
assembly_test: preview-assembly.jpg is a frame rebuilt only from the exported PNGs, layout.json numbers and the OFL fonts (assemble.py), as proof the kit is complete for the left-column roster, strips, verb plate, pill, objective line, ticker and a live scene card.
